approach:
Fix the class at its two origins. (A) Origin in the run: `Athena::dispatch` commits the job record and brief (run/mod.rs:1249-1257), then every later `?` (plan_round 1314, produce_and_verify 1335, close_dispatched) returns Err with no outcome. `RealSteps::run` turns that Err into `Run{outcome: None}` (drain.rs:4395-4408) and the drain moves on. Fix: wrap the post-commit part of `dispatch`. An error that is not a deliberate hold (LowDisk, SlotWait, BudgetShort), with the kill switch off and no resume mark, now closes the job `failed` with a stated reason through the existing `close_dispatched`, keeping the invocations it left (via `recover_interrupted`). Holds, a stop, and a job with a kept candidate stay dispatched, as today. (B) Origin in the listing: `steward::interrupted_work` keeps only the cli/steward channels (steward.rs:467) and hides every job that any later request retries (448-460), whatever became of that retry; status uses `retries_by_job`, where a dropped retry does not stand (retry.rs:246-267). Fix: drop the channel filter for interrupted jobs only, reuse `retries_by_job`, and add a pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, running, held, final_pass)`. It returns Close or Hold per dispatched request job with no process. A defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted(final_pass)` hook runs it before `queue()` (closes originals whose retry ended, and request-less jobs) and after `sweep` (adds a Hold line, with a reason, for every dispatched job still without an outcome). `prepare` drops the incomplete plan entry of an interrupted item. status.rs is not edited: `state_name`/`scan_jobs` already list every dispatched job with no process; tests pin it. The six live jobs get operator commands against the live records, outside the diff.

Cause of the six, from the code (not from their records, which are absent): the two origins above, one of which applies to each job. Records show job.json + brief-producer.md, no invocation, no outcome — the exact shape of an Err or a process death between the Dispatch commit and the producer's closing commit (invocations are committed only in the closing commit).

decisions.choice: Close a job whose run errors after the Dispatch commit, inside `dispatch`, with outcome `failed` and reason `stopped by an error after dispatch, before the job closed: <redacted error>`, via the existing `close_dispatched` with a `Closing` whose `new_invocations` are the invocations recovered from the state directory.
decisions.reason: This is the fault's origin (run/mod.rs:1314, 1335, 1342-1345: `finish_dispatched` calls `close_dispatched` only on Ok). `failed` follows the precedent of `stop_planning` (planning.rs:8-14), which already ends a job that stopped before the producer as failed with verification unknown; a failed job can be retried (retry.rs:38-47), an abandoned one cannot. `dispatch` holds the job lock, so `Athena::close` (manage.rs:96) cannot be called from there; `close_dispatched` can. Recovered invocations keep the cost of the aborted attempt on the books.

rejected.why: Closes as `abandoned`, which `earlier_attempt_with` refuses to retry (retry.rs:38-47), so the request would be lost to the drain.

rejected.option: Leave the job dispatched and rely on the next drain to retry it
rejected.why: A deterministic error would grow one dispatched retry per drain with no outcome. The brief requires an outcome with a reason.

rejected.option: Close every Err including holds and stops
rejected.why: SlotWait, LowDisk and BudgetShort are deliberate holds a later drain resumes (close.rs:170-212, run/mod.rs:481-490). The kill switch (lib.rs:268) and a kept candidate (`write_resume_mark`, producer.rs/mod.rs:1813) are resumable too. Closing would destroy work.

Only the post-commit section is wrapped; pre-commit errors (run_pin_tests.rs:350-363, 695-716) are untouched.
decisions.reason: Keeps every deliberate hold and every resumable job as a hold, as the critic asked, and leaves 'nothing was committed' errors alone.

rejected.why: A kill-switch stop mid-planning has no candidate but is a stop, not a failure.

decisions.choice: Drop the channel filter in `interrupted_work` only, and exclude jobs for which `reading::retries_by_job` has a standing retry. Keep `DRAINED_CHANNELS` in `queued_work` (steward.rs:414).
decisions.reason: A queued request on another channel may belong to another consumer; a dispatched job with no registry process belongs to nobody. Using `retries_by_job` gives drain the definition status already uses (status.rs:913), so a dropped retry no longer hides the original.

decisions.choice: New pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, running, held, final_pass) -> Vec<Settlement>` (`Close{job,why}` / `Hold{job,why}`), called through a defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted(final_pass) -> Vec<String>`. `RealSteps` implements it with `Athena::close`.
decisions.reason: A pure function over `Records` is unit-tested without a model. A defaulted trait method leaves every test stub unedited, as `reclaim_interrupted` does (drain.rs:576). `Athena::close` already recovers invocations, scores, cleans and commits under the gate, and takes the job lock, so a running job is refused.

rejected.why: `queue()` is also used by `athena plan`, which must stay read-only.
Touches athena-data, the gate and round-trip tests for no gain.

decisions.choice: Population and rules of `settle_interrupted` (answers the 'no request record' finding). It looks only at `records.request_jobs()` in state Dispatched with `!running(job)`. (1) `held(job)` is Some (a disk or slot marker from `disk::read_any_hold`, run/mod.rs:481-490): Hold, with the marker text and 'the next drain resumes it'; never Close. (2) No request record (a request job whose request.json is missing, so `athena retry` refuses it, retry.rs:54-56): Close with reason 'dispatched with no request record; it cannot be retried'. (3) A standing retry (`retries_by_job`), followed through interrupted retries to depth `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH`: if the last retry is closed, Close every interrupted job in the chain with reason `re-queued as <retry>, which ended <state>`; if it is open, Hold 'retried as <retry>, still <state>'. (4) No standing retry and `final_pass == false`: nothing, since the drain is about to retry it. (5) No standing retry and `final_pass == true`: Hold 'dispatched with no outcome and no process; not worked in this drain (job limit, budget, stop, or its retry could not be read); `athena retry <job>` resumes it, `athena close <job> --why ...` closes it'.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 2 and 5. Case 5 makes the drain report every job it left behind with a reason; cases 1 and 2 name the exact population and keep holds from being closed.

rejected.option: Close every dispatched job without a standing retry at the end of the drain
rejected.why: Discards resumable work; resuming is the first choice.

decisions.choice: Make `REQUEUE_CLOSE_REASON` in hestia.rs `pub(crate)` and use it from steward for the prefix of the settle reason. Add a hestia unit test that a job closed by `settle` with that reason is not `closed_by_person`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4: one constant, so a change to hestia's text cannot drift from steward's. It is a one-word visibility change with no behavior change; hestia's own tests at hestia.rs:4172 and 4386 stay as they are. The error close (decision 1) is a `failed` outcome, which `closed_by_person` (hestia.rs:346-356) does not match.

rejected.option: Duplicate the literal and pin it with a steward test
rejected.why: The pin cannot see hestia's constant, so a change on hestia's side goes unnoticed.

decisions.choice: In `Drain::prepare`, remove the incomplete plan entry of an interrupted item so its retry re-reads the request. Do not read it or close it.
decisions.reason: The first attempt for an interrupted item is `athena retry`, which reads the request again (drain.rs:1860), so the old plan fields are irrelevant; `Plan::build_improving` refuses an incomplete entry otherwise.

rejected.why: Spends a model call on a job the retry reads again.

decisions.choice: Leave status.rs, reading/retry.rs and the rest of run/ unedited; pin status with a test.

decisions.choice: Real-steps and core tests use two stop seams: (a) a script that makes the live-record write fail inside the first agent invocation after the Dispatch commit; (b) the existing `interrupt` helper for a process death.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3: (a) is a real stop between the Dispatch commit and the producer's closing commit. `StateDir::write_live` (state.rs:191-198) calls `create_dir_all` on the parent of `live/<path>`, so a script that plants a regular file named `records` in `StateDir::live_dir(job)` (state.rs:115) makes `invoke_and_record` return Err (invocation.rs:259-260). With `[job_plan]` the first invocation is the planner, so no producer ever runs. (b) copies the shape of a restart.

rejected.why: It copies the record shape, not the event.

risks.risk: The error close ends a job as failed that a later drain would have resumed, for example an error caused by a transient fault.
risks.mitigation: Only errors with no hold type, no kill switch and no kept candidate are closed (resume mark absent). The outcome is `failed`, so `athena retry` / the drain's failure handling can run it again from the request. A hold or a built candidate stays dispatched and is resumed.

risks.risk: An infrastructure error counts as a failed job in introspection and the scope guard, which could pause a line after repeated errors.
risks.mitigation: This matches the existing `stop_planning` precedent (planning.rs:8-14). The reason carries a fixed prefix so a person can tell it from a verifier failure. The question is raised in open_questions.

risks.risk: The reason text of the error may carry a secret or a machine path.
risks.mitigation: The reason is passed through `ctx.redactor.redact` before it is committed; if redaction fails, a fixed text without the error is used. Test with a path in the error.

risks.risk: `close_dispatched` itself fails (the commit is refused), so the job stays dispatched.
risks.mitigation: The original error is returned with the second error added as context, as today. The next drain lists the job (interrupted) and the final-pass settle reports it with a reason.

risks.risk: Closing an original too early could lose work or retry it twice.
risks.mitigation: Settle closes only when the standing retry (followed through interrupted retries) has an outcome. An open retry gives a Hold note. A held job (disk or slot marker) is never closed. Unit tests cover running, held, open, closed and chained cases; a drain test asserts the retried original is not retried twice.

risks.risk: `retries_by_job` treats an abandoned retry as not standing, so closing a middle job could re-list its parent for a second retry.
risks.mitigation: The settle follows the chain and closes every interrupted job in it in one pass, with a depth cap like `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH`. A Z-A-B unit test covers it.

risks.risk: Resuming off-channel jobs reverses a documented rule and an existing test.
risks.mitigation: The rewrite is explicit and named in the CHANGELOG. `queued_work` keeps its filter, pinned by a new test. The change applies only to dispatched jobs with no registry process.

risks.risk: Closing during a parallel drain races with a worker.
risks.mitigation: Settle errors become notes and never fail the drain. `close` takes the job lock and refuses a job another process runs. The final call comes after all workers finish (after `sweep`).

risks.risk: The core error test depends on `create_dir_all` failing when a regular file stands where a directory is needed. This holds for root as well, so a file mode is not what it relies on.
risks.mitigation: The test asserts the Err first happened by checking the closing reason and the recovered planner invocation, so a test where the write silently succeeds would fail the assertions and not pass vacuously.

risks.risk: The `interrupt` helper leaves the history one commit short, which differs from a real process death.
risks.mitigation: It is used only for the restart shape. Each test asserts the job has no invocation and no outcome before the drain; the error-path tests (a) use the real code path. If the shapes cannot be separated, `go_with_disk` (tests/drain.rs:2424) leaves a dispatched job with a hold marker, which exercises the Hold case.

risks.risk: The six outcomes cannot be written by the diff because records/ is excluded.
risks.mitigation: The diff holds only code, tests and CHANGELOG. Demonstration 4 is an operator step after merge, with each close citing a hash found by reading the job's brief and git log.

risks.risk: The expected-deliverables list names status.rs and reading/retry.rs, which this plan does not edit.
risks.mitigation: Not editing them is safe: status.rs already lists every dispatched job (tests pin it) and `retries_by_job` is reused unchanged. The run/mod.rs change is the wrapper described above. The CHANGELOG entry says status was left unchanged.

demonstrations.method: Three layers. (1) Core test in run/tests.rs `an_error_after_dispatch_before_the_producer_closes_the_job_with_the_reason`: `repo_with_planning(1)` and `athena_with`; the planning script plants the blocking file when `spec.role == Role::Planner`. `athena.go` returns `Finished`, `state == Failed`, a reason starting `stopped by an error after dispatch`. Records: the job is Closed(Failed), has job.json and brief-producer.md, a planner invocation recovered from the usage file, and no producer invocation. Same file: `a_low_disk_hold_after_dispatch_is_not_closed_by_the_error_path` (the existing hold tests at 3550, 4098, 4694 and 4806 also still expect Err), and `an_error_after_dispatch_with_the_kill_switch_on_leaves_the_job_dispatched` (calls `athena.stop()` in the script, manage.rs:499). (2) tests/drain.rs real-steps: `drain_resumes_an_interrupted_job_on_any_channel` (rewrite of the test at 5122): a cli and a web job are interrupted with `interrupt`, each asserted dispatched with no invocation and no outcome. The drain retries both; both originals end Closed(Abandoned) with a reason starting `re-queued as <retry>`. Also `a_run_that_errors_after_dispatch_ends_with_an_outcome_in_the_same_drain`: a producer-role script plants the blocking file, the drain runs, and the report line names the job with the failure reason, with the job closed Failed. Also `an_interrupted_job_whose_retry_was_dropped_is_listed_again` and `an_interrupted_job_with_a_landed_retry_is_closed_by_the_drain`. (3) steward unit tests `settle_*`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core run::tests::an_error_after_dispatch && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- interrupted && cargo test --locked -p athena-core steward::tests::settle
demonstrations.observes: Each stopped job ends with an outcome record carrying a stated reason, or is resumed by a passing retry in the drain. The drain notes carry the `closed <job>: <why>` lines.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the dispatch wrapper, `go` returns Err and the job stays dispatched with no outcome, so the core and drain error tests fail. Without the new `interrupted_work`, the web job is not listed and stays dispatched. A job whose retry was dropped is never re-listed, and a job whose retry landed stays dispatched.

Fixtures: core `athena_with`/`repo_with_planning`/`planning_script` (run/tests.rs:187, 287, 1189), exist; `Fixture::new()`, `killing_producer`, `interrupt`, `request_on` (tests/drain.rs:5094, 5108, 4968), exist. The doubles are the scripted agent and `RecordingLander`; the listing, settle and error-close logic is production code. demonstrations.method: Tests: (a) real-steps `drain_leaves_no_dispatched_job_without_an_outcome_or_a_note`: two interrupted cli jobs, `Limits{max_jobs: 1,..}`. The first is retried and passes, and its original is closed. The second is not worked. Assert that after the drain every request job is closed, or is Dispatched and named in `report.notes` with a line starting `held <job>:` that carries a reason and the `athena retry` hint. (b) Stub `drain_works_an_interrupted_item_whose_plan_entry_is_incomplete`: Stub with `interrupted: vec!["a"]` and a plan entry missing its rung; the log is `reread a`, `run a-retry`, and a note says the retry reads the request again. (c) Stub `drain_notes_what_settling_interrupted_jobs_did`: new `Stub.settled` field; both the start call (`final_pass=false`) and the end call (`true`) reach `Report::notes`. (d) Stub: an interrupted item held by `paused` still gets its pass-over line. (e) Unit tests: a held job (disk or slot marker) gets Hold, never Close; a request-less job gets Close with a reason; with `final_pass=false` a job with no standing retry yields nothing; with `final_pass=true` it yields a Hold with a reason.
demonstrations.observes: The drain retries the item, closes it with a reason, or reports it held with a reason in its notes. No dispatched job is silently left.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the final-pass Hold, test (a) finds the second job dispatched with no note. Without the plan-entry exemption, (b) shows item a refused as not worked and never reread. Without the hook, (c) finds no notes.
demonstrations.seam: `drain::drain` against `Stub` (tests/drain.rs:127, exists) extended with a `settled` field and its `settle_interrupted` impl (added by the step that edits the Stub); `Limits.max_jobs` exists (drain.rs:288-294; `limits()` at tests/drain.rs:332); real-steps fixture as in criterion 1. The double supplies only the world; the settle selection is steward code, the exemption and notes are drain.rs code.

demonstrations.method: Test `status_lists_every_dispatched_job_with_no_outcome_whatever_its_channel`: interrupt a cli job and a web job. Call `athena.status()` and assert both ids are in `view.open` with state interrupted and an `athena retry <id>` next line, and that `display::status(&view)` contains each id. Add a third job dispatched with a held marker and assert it is listed too. Then run the drain and assert neither original is in `open` (both closed with a reason). Existing tests/retry.rs 1031, 1072, 1110 and 1139 keep passing.
demonstrations.observes: Status lists every dispatched job with no outcome and no process, with its id and a next-step line. After the drain none of them remain open.

open_questions: User: May a job that was interrupted and whose standing retry ended rejected or failed be closed as abandoned with the reason `re-queued as <retry>, which ended <state>`? The plan does so, because the retry carries the work forward and the original would otherwise stay dispatched for ever. The alternative is to leave it listed as 'retried as X' until a person closes it.

User: Should an error after dispatch with no kept candidate close the job as `failed` (retryable and counted by introspection and the scope guard, as `stop_planning` does) or as `abandoned` (not counted, but `athena retry` refuses it)? The plan uses `failed`.
